movement_source: row 'Net profit excluding Notable Items', column Full Year Sept 2024 -> column Full Year Sept 2025
headline: Westpac's FY25 net profit excluding Notable Items (its cash-comparable headline measure) was $6,972m, down 2% from $7,113m; statutory net profit was $6,916m, down 1% - the gap is Notable Items, a $56m post-tax hedging reduction in FY25 vs $123m in FY24. Net operating income rose 3% to $22,464m ($21.8bn to $22.5bn), but pre-provision profit fell 3% to $10,548m: the bank's own summary is that 'higher operating income and lower credit impairment charges more than offset by higher expenses' drove the profit decline. Bridge ($m, FY25 vs FY24): NII +557 (up 3% to $19,473m; AIEA +3% to $1,002,856m, business loans +11%; NIM -1bp to 1.94%; T&M income -2% to $1,282m); other operating income +144 (up 5% to $2,991m; fees +4% to $1,732m, wealth +8% to $476m, trading/other +7% to $783m); UNDERLYING operating expenses -699 (ex-restructuring +6% to $11,643m; staff +$427m to $6,326m; technology +$372m to $3,136m on UNITE, wages, software amortisation); restructuring charge -273 (Fit for Growth, FY24 nil); credit impairment +113 (charges $424m, 5bps vs 7bps; write-backs +$102m, recoveries +$57m, partly offset by CAP +$61m); tax & NCI +17 (ETR 31.0% vs 30.8%; NCI -$17m). Sum: -141.

drivers.narrative: Bank: NII 'increased 3% to $19,473 million'. Core NII +3% to $18,191m - 'Balance sheet growth was partly offset by lower net interest margin'. AIEA +3% to $1,002,856m (business loans +11%, housing +2%); NIM -1bp to 1.94%; Treasury & Markets income -2% to $1,282m on stronger prior-year Treasury.

drivers.narrative: Up 5% to $2,991m: net fee income +4% to $1,732m on 'an increase in card fees and higher business and Institutional lending fees from a larger balance sheet'; net wealth management +8% to $476m on higher funds under administration; trading and other +7% to $783m on higher sales and risk management income including rates and FX.

drivers.narrative: UNDERLYING operating expenses excluding the $273m restructuring charge: +6% to $11,643m. Staff +$427m to $6,326m (wage growth, UNITE, investment in bankers; average FTE +1%); technology +$372m to $3,136m (UNITE ramp-up, higher software amortisation, maintenance/licences); occupancy -$48m to $652m and other -$52m to $1,529m. Expense-to-income 53.0% vs 50.3%. Pack walk: productivity -$402m and investments +$359m (UNITE $399m).

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 vs Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Fit for Growth restructuring charge of $273m (Second Half 2025) 'to support targeted productivity initiatives'; FY24: nil. The bank presents it INSIDE operating expenses - its official Notable Items table shows Large items nil and only hedging items - so it is stated separately here per bridge method, never inside the underlying expense number.

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 vs Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Charges down 21% to $424m = 5bps of average loans vs 7bps. 'Mainly due to an increase in write-backs and recoveries partly offset by a higher CAP charge': write-backs +$102m to $195m, recoveries +$57m to $247m, new IAPs -$15m to $408m; CAP charge +$61m to $458m (write-offs $561m, other-CAP benefit $103m; overlays balance +$59m). Mortgage 90+ delinquencies 1.05% to 0.70%.

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 vs Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Income tax expense -$34m to $3,135m: effective tax rate 31.0% vs 30.8%, 'mainly due to benefits from prior period tax adjustments in Full Year 2024 not repeated in Full Year 2025'. Profit attributable to NCI -$17m (FY24: nil). Net +$17m, matching the bridge's 'Tax & NCI' bar.

notable_items: Fit for Growth restructuring charge $273m sits inside FY25 operating expenses (FY24: nil); WBC's official Notable Items definition excludes it (large items nil) - claimed as a separate component per bridge method, never inside underlying opex
Official Notable Items (post tax) were hedging items only: $56m reduction FY25 vs $123m reduction FY24 - a statutory-to-cash reconciliation item, not a driver of the cash-comparable movement
NCI of $17m in FY25 vs nil in FY24, folded into tax_and_other

Notable items detail: unrealised fair value loss on hedges of accrual-accounted term funding $43m FY25 (2024: $128m reduction); net ineffectiveness on qualifying hedges $13m reduction FY25 (2024: $5m benefit)
limitations: Plan item 'results announcement bridge/waterfall chart': the results announcement publishes NO graphical FY24-FY25 waterfall; its p9 performance-summary table with FY movement columns and narrative serves that role, and the graphical walk lives in the investor discussion pack p40 (adopted; bars equal the results table movements exactly).

Plan item 'pack NIM and volume (AIEA) drivers': the pack's EARNINGS DRIVERS section (p39) is a section divider with no content; the NIM walk (loans -1bp, deposits -2bps, liquid assets +2bps, wholesale funding -1bp, capital & other +1bp, T&M flat) and AIEA detail were read from the results announcement pp11-12, corroborated by the pack's p40 chart annotation (ev-2).

Plan item 'pack expense and impairment commentary': expense commentary and the FY24-FY25 expense waterfall come from the pack (pp20, 27). The pack's impairment pages (pp29, 49) decompose the 2H25-vs-1H25 half-on-half movement, not the FY24-FY25 movement, so the FY impairment decomposition is cited from the results announcement p21.
No cash earnings measure published since 1H23; the headline row is Net profit excluding Notable Items, treated as cash-comparable and flagged as such throughout.
Volume/margin are not separately quantified in $m for FY25-vs-FY24, so NII is claimed as one total; the bps NIM decomposition is context only.
NCI (-$17m) is folded into tax_and_other to match the bank's 'Tax & NCI' bar; the tax expense movement alone is +$34m.

The $273m restructuring charge is NOT a Notable Item under WBC's published definition (Notable Items = hedging items only; large items nil); it is broken out separately per the bridge method, so underlying opex here ($11,643m) differs from the bank's Notable-Items-basis expenses by that line only.

Statutory (-1%) vs ex-notables (-2%) differ because the hedging Notable Items swing was +$67m favourable (a $56m reduction vs $123m); these unrealised hedging fair-value items explain the statutory-cash gap in the same period, not the year-on-year cash-comparable movement.
The auto finance portfolio sale (March 2025) affected AIEA growth and loan spreads; the bank discloses no separate $ contribution, so no standalone driver is claimed.

Impairment relief is net: write-backs/recoveries gains (+$159m combined) sit against a higher CAP charge (+$61m) that includes +$59m of overlays - the +$113m is a net figure, as the bank itself qualifies ('partly offset by').
Basis normalised from 'cash' to 'ex_notables': no page in evidence prints 'cash' beside the movement, and the registry names ex_notables as the bank's headline basis.
